sentences.text: Sikannisuchus was an extinct genus of large archosaurs that grew to approximately four meters in length.
Scientists know this animal from the holotype — the specimen the species is based on — TMP 94.382.3, which includes a rear section of the skull roof and other broken pieces.
Fossils were discovered at four sites in the Pardonet Formation near Sikanni Chief. Elizabeth L. Nicholls, Donald B. Brinkman, and Xiao-Chun Wu named the genus Sikannisuchus huskyi in 1998.
Taxonomically, Sikannisuchus belongs to the order Archosauria, the subclass Archosauromorpha, and the class Reptilia.
This creature lived during the Norian stage of the Triassic, between 227.3 and 205.7 million years ago. Its fossils share the Pardonet Formation with ichthyosaurs, coelacanths, and various molluscs.
